high.title: Interest Rate Cooling Down, Experts Point Out 2 Main Impacts on Stock Market
high.summary: Recently, many commercial banks have simultaneously reduced both deposit and lending rates, reversing the upward trend that lasted from late 2025. This move has quickly attracted market attention, especially as investors seek new supportive signals for capital flows. According to Nguyen Trong Dinh Tam, Director of Individual Customer Investment Advisory Division at Thien Viet Securities (TVS), the rate cuts could bring two main effects: First, creating positive psychological effects in the short term for interest rate-sensitive stock groups such as residential real estate, construction, and securities. Second, facilitating capital flows back to the stock market, especially when valuations of many stocks have become more attractive compared to the 5-year average after recent volatility. The expert noted that the current rate reduction trend may only be short-term, as maintaining a prolonged low interest rate cycle would depend on multiple factors.

high.title: "Any Dramatic Variables from the World Can Cause VN-Index to Fluctuate Strongly"
high.summary: The stock market has experienced an emotional week of trading with an explosive breakthrough on Wednesday (8/4), with VN-Index surging nearly 80 points with purple spreading widely. According to analyst Vu Thi Quynh Trang from Pinetree Securities, the momentum that caused VN-Index to explode came from three main factors: (1) Government apparatus completion - new PM Le Minh Hung officially took office with the message of treating GDP growth above 10% as a "development mandate," and new SBV Governor directed commercial banks to commit to reducing interest rates by 0.5%-1% to stabilize the macro economy; (2) FTSE Russell confirmed the roadmap to upgrade Vietnam to emerging market status in September 2026, creating great confidence for foreign capital flows; (3) Middle East tensions eased through a 2-week ceasefire agreement between the US and Iran, causing world oil prices to plummet by over 15%, helping relieve global inflation pressure. Technically, the strong rally created a large gap up in the 1,677-1,705 point range, with profit-taking pressure expected at higher levels.

high.title: "Vitamin Shot" for the Stock Market
high.summary: Immediately after the meeting with the State Bank led by Governor Pham Duc An, a series of commercial banks simultaneously reduced deposit and lending rates. This move quickly attracted market attention as investors expect cooling interest rates to create new momentum for capital flows. According to Tran Quoc Toan, Director of Branch 2 Head Office at Mirae Asset Securities (MAS), rate cuts can be seen as a direct "vitamin shot" for the market. First, the stock market is expected to become attractive again - when deposit rates are no longer sufficiently attractive after the recent deposit race, idle funds from households and institutions will tend to shift to assets with higher returns, with securities being the top choice. Second, cooling interest rates help improve corporate profit margins by reducing borrowing costs, especially benefiting interest rate-sensitive sectors like real estate, construction, and banking.

high.title: Bank Executives Forecast Interest Rates After Multiple Banks' Moves
high.summary: On April 12, more commercial banks joined the rate reduction wave for both deposits and loans. Agribank announced a sharp 0.5 percentage point cut in deposit rates for terms from 24 months and above for individual customers, effective from April 13, 2026. After adjustment, the highest deposit rate at Agribank is 6%/year for 24-month terms and 5.9% for 12-18 month terms. Agribank also reduced lending rates by 0.5 percentage points. According to bank representatives, reducing both deposit and lending rates simultaneously aims to share capital costs with customers as the economy needs additional momentum for recovery and growth. Nam A Bank also announced cuts to both deposit and lending rates following the banking sector meeting led by Governor Pham Duc An, with deposit rate reductions up to 0.5 percentage points for terms from 6 months and above.

high.title: Over 20 Banks Simultaneously Cut Interest Rates: Agribank, Vietcombank, VietinBank, BIDV and Many Large Banks Join
high.summary: According to statistics, as of this morning, over 20 banks have reduced deposit rates, including: BIDV, VietinBank, OCB, ACB, MB, VPBank, SeABank, Vietcombank, BVBank, Techcombank, Sacombank, Eximbank, LPBank, SHB, TPBank, ABBank, KienlongBank, BaoViet Bank, Nam A Bank, NCB, Viet A Bank, and Agribank. Reduction ranges from 0.1-0.5%/year at many banks. Vietcombank cut 0.5%/year for 24-month terms; VietinBank, BIDV and Agribank reduced 0.5%/year for terms from 24 months and above. Techcombank cut 0.1%/year for short terms of 3-5 months and up to 0.5%/year for 6-36 month terms. This coordinated rate reduction follows the State Bank meeting and signals significant monetary policy easing to support economic growth and capital market flows.

medium.title: Securities Receive "Double Boost", VN-Index Expected to Head Toward 1,770 Points
medium.summary: MB Securities (MBS) reports that as Middle East geopolitical tensions shift from temporary peace to more sustainable agreements, the domestic stock market is receiving a "double boost" from both international factors (US-Iran ceasefire reducing geopolitical risk, global stocks surging) and domestic factors (leadership completion + FTSE upgrade + 17 banks cutting rates by up to 1%/year after SBV-bank meeting). MBS expects recovery to continue as the government aggressively implements solutions to maintain economic growth targets, with VN-Index successfully creating a bottom around MA200 support.

medium.title: FTSE Representative: Billions of USD About to Flow Into Vietnam and No More "Hit and Run"
medium.summary: At an SSI webinar, Wanming Du from FTSE Russell confirmed Vietnam has met all criteria for Secondary Emerging Market status, likely achieving this around September 2026. The transition will occur over 4 phases across one year to ensure operational factors, liquidity, and investor requirements are met. She emphasized that the upgrade will bring structural, long-term capital flows rather than sudden speculative money, providing more sustainable market development.

medium.title: Good News for Vietcombank Users When Traveling
medium.summary: Vietcombank launched cross-border QR payment services through partnership with Alipay+, allowing customers to use the VCB Digibank app for payments in over 50 countries including China, South Korea, Singapore, Malaysia, and countries in Europe and Americas. This eliminates the need for currency exchange or carrying cash when traveling abroad, making international spending seamless.

medium.title: First Time in Vietnam: Using Domestic Banking App to Scan QR for Payments When Traveling to China, South Korea, Singapore...
medium.summary: Following the QR payment expansion between Vietnam-China for Chinese tourists to Vietnam, Vietcombank launched cross-border QR payment services for Vietnamese customers in over 50 countries. This is particularly significant for travel to China where QR payments are ubiquitous and cash/international cards are less accepted.

medium.title: Gold Ring and Gold Bar Prices on 12/4
medium.summary: Domestic gold prices remained sideways at the session start on 12/4. SJC gold bars traded at 169.7-172.7 million VND/tael across major brands. Gold rings at SJC were 169.4-172.4 million VND/tael, while PNJ quoted 169.2-172.2 million VND/tael. International gold closed the week at $4,747/ounce, up nearly 1.6% for the third consecutive weekly gain as USD weakened following US-Iran ceasefire, despite trader skepticism about ceasefire durability.

medium.title: SJC Gold Bar and Gold Ring Prices This Afternoon 13/4
medium.summary: Afternoon update 13/4 shows SJC gold bars quoted at 168.5-171.5 million VND/tael across major brands. Gold rings at DOJI, Bao Tin Minh Chau, Bao Tin Manh Hai also at 168.5-171.5 million VND/tael, while SJC and PNJ applied 168.2-171.2 million VND/tael. Compared to morning, SJC gold fell 900,000 VND/tael, reflecting continued volatility in precious metals markets.
